chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: Which conformation of methylcyclohexane is thermodynamically favored at 25°C?

options.label: A
options.text: Chair conformation with the methyl group in the equatorial position (95% abundance)

options.label: B
options.text: Chair conformation with the methyl group in the axial position

options.label: C
options.text: Planar flat cyclohexane ring

options.label: D
options.text: Boat conformation with flagpole methyl interaction

questions.correct_answer: Chair conformation with the methyl group in the equatorial position (95% abundance)
questions.explanation: Equatorial methyl avoids destabilizing 1,3-diaxial steric interactions with axial ring hydrogens.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: What structural factor causes the energy penalty of an axial substituent on cyclohexane?

options.label: A
options.text: Torsional strain from eclipsed C-C bonds

options.label: B
options.text: Steric clash (gauche-like interactions) with the two syn-axial hydrogens on carbons 3 and 5

options.label: C
options.text: Angle strain from deviation from 109.5° tetrahedral angles

options.label: D
options.text: Dipole-dipole repulsion with ring carbons

questions.correct_answer: Steric clash (gauche-like interactions) with the two syn-axial hydrogens on carbons 3 and 5
questions.explanation: Axial substituents experience steric crowding with axial hydrogens positioned two carbons away on the same face.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: What is the most stable conformation of trans-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane?

options.label: A
options.text: Diequatorial (1e, 2e) chair conformation

options.label: B
options.text: Axial-equatorial (1a, 2e) chair conformation

options.label: C
options.text: Twist-boat conformation

options.label: D
options.text: Diaxial (1a, 2a) chair conformation

questions.correct_answer: Diequatorial (1e, 2e) chair conformation
questions.explanation: The trans-1,2 isomer can place both methyl groups in equatorial positions simultaneously.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: What are the positions of the methyl groups in the chair conformations of cis-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane?

options.label: A
options.text: One axial and one equatorial (1a, 2e), interconverting to (1e, 2a) upon ring flip

options.label: B
options.text: Both diequatorial (1e, 2e)

options.label: C
options.text: Both planar in the ring plane

options.label: D
options.text: Both diaxial (1a, 2a)

questions.correct_answer: One axial and one equatorial (1a, 2e), interconverting to (1e, 2a) upon ring flip
questions.explanation: In the 1,2-cis isomer, one substituent must point up (axial) and the other up (equatorial).

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: What is the stereochemical nature of cis-1,3-dimethylcyclohexane?

options.label: A
options.text: It is an achiral meso compound possessing an internal plane of symmetry

options.label: B
options.text: It is a constitutional isomer of 1,4-dimethylcyclohexane

options.label: C
options.text: It is an optically active diastereomer

options.label: D
options.text: It is a chiral molecule with two enantiomers

questions.correct_answer: It is an achiral meso compound possessing an internal plane of symmetry
questions.explanation: An internal vertical symmetry plane bisects C2 and C5, rendering cis-1,3-dimethylcyclohexane achiral (meso).

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: Why is trans-1,4-di-tert-butylcyclohexane considered a conformationally locked ring?

options.label: A
options.text: The massive A-value of tert-butyl groups (~20 kJ/mol) locks both groups into equatorial positions

options.label: B
options.text: The tert-butyl groups form an intramolecular covalent bond

options.label: C
options.text: It exists exclusively in a stable twist-boat conformation

options.label: D
options.text: The ring is planar and cannot undergo chair flips

questions.correct_answer: The massive A-value of tert-butyl groups (~20 kJ/mol) locks both groups into equatorial positions
questions.explanation: The extreme energy cost of placing even one tert-butyl axial locks the molecule in the diequatorial chair.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: Why does cyclopropane possess 115 kJ/mol of ring strain?

options.label: A
options.text: 1,3-Diaxial steric repulsion across the ring

options.label: B
options.text: Non-coplanar p-orbital misalignment

options.label: C
options.text: Severe angle strain (60° bond angles vs 109.5° tetrahedral) combined with eclipsing C-H torsional strain

options.label: D
options.text: Unfavorable dipole moments

questions.correct_answer: Severe angle strain (60° bond angles vs 109.5° tetrahedral) combined with eclipsing C-H torsional strain
questions.explanation: Carbons are forced into rigid 60° 'bent' bonds with all six C-H bonds eclipsed.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: What two factors make the cyclohexane boat conformation 29 kJ/mol higher in energy than the chair?

options.label: A
options.text: Severe dipole-dipole repulsions

options.label: B
options.text: 1,3-Diaxial interactions with axial substituents

options.label: C
options.text: Angle strain at all six carbon vertices

options.label: D
options.text: Flagpole steric interactions between C1/C4 hydrogens and torsional strain from eclipsed bonds along the sides

questions.correct_answer: Flagpole steric interactions between C1/C4 hydrogens and torsional strain from eclipsed bonds along the sides
questions.explanation: The boat has four pairs of eclipsed C-H bonds and steric clash between the two inside flagpole hydrogens.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: How do cis-decalin and trans-decalin differ in conformational flexibility?

options.label: A
options.text: trans-Decalin is rigidly locked and cannot ring-flip; cis-decalin is conformationally flexible and undergoes chair flips

options.label: B
options.text: cis-Decalin is planar; trans-decalin is non-planar

options.label: C
options.text: Both decalins have identical heats of combustion

options.label: D
options.text: trans-Decalin is a meso compound; cis-decalin is chiral

questions.correct_answer: trans-Decalin is rigidly locked and cannot ring-flip; cis-decalin is conformationally flexible and undergoes chair flips
questions.explanation: trans-Decalin is fused via diequatorial bonds which cannot flip without tearing bonds; cis-decalin can flip chairs.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: What does a substituent's conformational A-value represent in cyclohexane chemistry?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: The rate constant of nucleophilic substitution

options.label: C
options.text: The free energy difference (-ΔG°) between the axial and equatorial chair conformations

questions.explanation: A-values quantitatively rank the steric preference of groups for the equatorial position.

questions.question: Why is trans-1,4-di-tert-butylcyclohexane considered a conformationally locked ring?

options.text: The tert-butyl groups form an intramolecular covalent bond

questions.correct_answer: The massive A-value of tert-butyl groups (~20 kJ/mol) locks both groups into equatorial positions

questions.question: How do cis-decalin and trans-decalin differ in conformational flexibility?

questions.correct_answer: trans-Decalin is rigidly locked and cannot ring-flip; cis-decalin is conformationally flexible and undergoes chair flips

questions.correct_answer: The free energy difference (-ΔG°) between the axial and equatorial chair conformations
questions.explanation: A-values quantitatively rank the steric preference of groups for the equatorial position.

questions.question: Which conformation of methylcyclohexane is thermodynamically favored at 25°C?

options.label: B
options.text: Planar flat cyclohexane ring

options.label: C
options.text: Chair conformation with the methyl group in the axial position

options.label: D
options.text: Boat conformation with flagpole methyl interaction

questions.correct_answer: Chair conformation with the methyl group in the equatorial position (95% abundance)
questions.explanation: Equatorial methyl avoids destabilizing 1,3-diaxial steric interactions with axial ring hydrogens.

questions.chapter_title: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry
questions.question: What structural factor causes the energy penalty of an axial substituent on cyclohexane?

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: Steric clash (gauche-like interactions) with the two syn-axial hydrogens on carbons 3 and 5

options.text: Dipole-dipole repulsion with ring carbons

questions.correct_answer: Steric clash (gauche-like interactions) with the two syn-axial hydrogens on carbons 3 and 5
questions.explanation: Axial substituents experience steric crowding with axial hydrogens positioned two carbons away on the same face.
